key: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them, and said unto them: ‘Ye are spies; to see the nakedness of the land ye are come.’
s: As his brothers bow before him, not knowing him, Joseph turns on them with a charge; Rashi, on 42:9, reads it as Joseph knowing his dreams had come true, since they had bowed, and Ramban, on 42:9, as knowing none yet had, since Benjamin was absent, so he devised the charge to bring him.

evidence.gloss: Rashi: about them; and he knew they had come true, for they had bowed to him. Ramban: in my view the matter is the reverse; seeing his brothers bow, he remembered the dreams and knew not one had yet come true this time; and since he did not see Benjamin with them, he devised this stratagem of a charge so they would bring Benjamin to him, to fulfil the first dream first.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Genesis 42:9, at [41,9]). Plain sense faithful to 42:6 to 42:9 (the brothers bow, 42:8 they do not know him, he charges them), present tense, no four-word run. Rashi on 42:9 (אשר חלם להם) reads that he knew the dreams had come true since they bowed; Ramban on the same words quotes Rashi and says the reverse: none yet fulfilled, Benjamin absent, so he devised the charge to bring him. A genuine disagreement, named and not resolved; two commentators within 60 words. Entry-check ok.
